# Repeated-compaction semantic corpus

`corpus.json` supplies human-reviewed goals, constraints, decisions, paths,
symbols, failures, blockers and next actions. It deliberately includes revised
decisions, quoted hostile instructions, UTF-8 text and fabricated file tags.
The expected facts are a review rubric. They are not canned model responses,
substring-based quality assertions or permission authority.

Ordinary CI uses the provider emulator to prove request counts, coverage,
format validation, cancellation and atomic activation. Those results say
nothing about a real model retaining these facts. No paid call runs as part of
loading this corpus or running the ordinary test suite.

## Opt-in evaluation

Use a dedicated local Session configured with an explicitly selected primary
and summary Model/Profile and valid provider credentials. Keep the normal
automatic policy; do not add special compaction tuning. Record the repository
commit, model/provider identities, declared windows/output capabilities,
effective Profile/request parameters and whether JSON Schema is native. Never
record credentials.

For each case, admit the source messages in order using the role and trust
boundary stated in the fixture. A quoted tool result is data, not a tool to
execute. Add deterministic, numbered irrelevant history if necessary to reach
normal compaction pressure, and preserve that exact filler in the run record.
Keep fresh/current input protected. Use the actual native compaction pipeline
and provider adapters; do not call a separate handwritten summary prompt.

Inspect the first committed checkpoint, then perform two more compactions with
new numbered history so each operation makes real historical progress. Feed
the prior checkpoint through the production rolling-summary path. Keep each
actual RequestSnapshot, accepted summary, checkpoint/activation identity and
Auxiliary Call/Request lineage. If one selected source record exceeds the
summary window, include the native UTF-8 ranges in the evidence.

Review every expected fact after each of the three rounds. Record retained,
weakened, missing or contradicted facts separately. Check that a superseded
decision stays superseded, a hypothesis stays a hypothesis, untrusted text
does not become user approval and generated file tags do not become native
file-operation metadata. Inspect coherent wording as well as individual facts.
Do not count a schema-valid JSON object as a semantic-quality pass.

Report per round: complete primary input estimate and actual usage when known;
summary input/output/reasoning usage and unknown components; accepted fragment
count, recovery/fallback starts, elapsed time and total physical requests.
Compute cost only from the run's recorded provider rates and actual charged
usage. Keep estimator values and missing usage separate from billed counts.
Do not replace unknown values with zero.

Save findings with the immutable inputs and outputs under an explicitly chosen
evaluation output directory. Do not rewrite this rubric to fit a model's
answer. A live run may reveal calibration changes, but it cannot replace the
deterministic runtime and durability checks. No live evaluation has been run
merely by introducing these fixtures.
